The noble warrior held his sword at the beggar's throat, the strong wind blowing his masterfully woven cape upwards on his back.

For you see Mythlon, now we find ourselves in a peculiar spot. Me with the mortal blade and you poor, miserable and defeated! I have stripped you of your rank, your home and your pride. You lay worthless and defeated beneath my feet! You have escaped me for far too long but you knew I was coming for you someday! Did you think your pathetic attempt to escape was gonna succeed against the mighty ruler of all the lands around you?!

You see, your majesty... The beggar's voice was raspy, his lungs full from the cold. Neither of us has won.

Yes, he continued. You have taken everything from me... but I also have, unfortunately, destroyed you. Look at you, a ruler of men, came all the way here to finish someone, as you say, worthless. I couldn't do you harm now even if I tried. You have all the riches and wants provided for in Nalingan Castle yet you find no joy in living - you have wasted all those years in vain, you have made your life's only goal to fight me even though you have settled our debts long ago. You're an empty person as well, much as I.

In this way, I have defeated you too, my lord. But it sure does not feel like victory.

The standing man's face was red with rage, his sword trembling wildly in his hands but still pointed at the traitor's neck.

You see, milord. I have forgiven you. I have taken the blame which is mine and counted my losses. I have run away not to escape your clutches but in the hope that with me gone you would forget all about this nonsense and move on. You are still young Michvt - go and live your life, forget about me. I'm done and counted for now, good bye and god speed.

Both of them remained quiet for a minute, Michvt's sword held down now. It took some thinking for him to finally realize the victory he yearned so long for was actually already in his hands for years now.

He sheathed his blade and started the journey back home, not even offering a last glance at his opponent. A few hours into the journey though he turned back, suddenly realizing he had left a friend behind, miserable and alone. He could not believe he had forgotten.

Roku throws a jab with a right swing, the blows blocked with Dr. Steiner's raised guards. A ruse to draw him into a false sense of security, broken immediately after the low kicks. Now the only thing left to do was to pound the opponent like a beach ball as much as possible before he could recover. The health bar shaved away like an ice pop held by someone's kiddie cousin, leaving just enough for the brutal finish. Roku's eyes and mouth glowed, giving way to the ultimate triple beam into Dr. Steiner's fallen body. There is no kill like overkill.

The screen blazed the caption "Perfect" and showed Roku standing straight with his tattered cloaked back to Dr. Steiner, thumbs down toward the pixelated crowd. Dr. Steiner, lying prone, raised his fists and said in pitiable tone, "You will pay for this arrogance!"

"Hey, that wasn't fair!" cried my 15th win of the day. I laid my hand upon my chest, basking in glory as I smiled.

"Well Sophia, that's why you don't challenge a pro, much less the champion."

"That's it! I'm not going to play with you anymore!" Sophia slid off stool, pushing it hard on the floor. I winced as the steel frame clanked against concrete. I got off of my seat gently and picked up the fallen stool, hoping the store manager wouldn't gripe at me for the noise.

"Hey, you're not mad, are you?" I asked, her back toward me.

"NO I'M NOT." I saw her hands come up to her face. "I'm going home." I frowned. She always act this way, denying that she was being emotional. Why couldn't she admit it for once that she was?

"Hey, it's not my fault that you're ..." I was about to say she was bad at the game, but my mind stopped myself. She swung around, making me raise my hands in surprise.

"That I'm what?" The way she looked at me with such contempt made my cheeks burn. "Huh? Answer me!" Why was she grilling me like this like I did something wrong? I went out of my way to spend time and quarters with her!

"Jeez, why are you such a sore loser?" I didn't care what I said. I was ticked off. I didn't deserve this.

Sophia clenched her fist and raised one like she was going to hit me. I glared, daring her to do so. Instead she turned and walked toward the door, her every step a stomp. She gave me one last look and stuck her tongue at me. I gave the door the finger after her face was gone.

I took my seat in front of the game station, preparing to play against a brutal difficulty AI. When I was about to press the start button however, I noticed the fight conclusion scene was looping. Dr. Steiner continued to raise his fist at the victorious Roku.

Sophia looked like she was going to cry. I didn't care, but I had a feeling that I would in a day. I didn't do anything wrong. There wasn't, shouldn't be a reason for me to feel bad. I didn't anyways, so that's that. I held a quarter in my hand, but I didn't insert it.

PLAY AGAIN? The countdown from 10 began. I let it go down to zero, watching Dr. Steiner comically promising Roku regret.

I knew where Sophia lived. I could probably find her if I tried. I held my head over the controls. I wasn't sure if I was ready to say sorry, or even knew what I was sorry for, but this wasn't worth it. Sophia was.

As I was getting ready to leave my seat, a hand slapped the back of head. I turned around looking angry, but as soon I as saw who it was, my blood ran cold like the ice pop held by someone's kiddie cousin.

"You were supposed to be back an hour ago with the eggs." My mother said, casting a shadow upon my stooled up body.

I swallowed. I didn't have enough quarters.

"I'm sorry." He said almost casually. "I honestly wish this could've ended in some other way."

Liar. I can see it from the smirk on your face. I opened my mouth to curse him - but no curses rang out. The only thing I could spit now was blood.

"Goodbye, brother dearest. Humanity will remember you for what you did for them." And with a slight, almost ironic bow, he began to saunter off towards the door.

As I wheezed and coughed, trying to draw air from a windpipe that just wasn't there, I began to remember the strangest of things - something I'd forgotten for a long time...

A similar scene, not so long ago, that seemed so faraway that it might've been from another world...

"Humans are scum." A cough, a rattling, choking noise as the old man spat out his blood. "They're worse than pigs." An ironic grin with teeth gritted so hard that I could almost hear them grinding.

"That's a lie, old man." I said, triumphant. "We defeated you."

A brief pause. Then a laugh - the most awful, hacking, dying laugh that I have ever heard in my entire life. "You'll see. Oh, you'll see. They stand united, now - but that won't last." Another fit of coughing - blood and phlegm caked his lips. "They could only have stopped their fighting because of me," he managed at last. "I was the one who kept them in peace. By acting... as their common... enemy..."

You're a liar. You're nothing but a villain. A delusional madman, who in his dying moments thinks that he was a hero...

But I said none of these things.

He was gone.

And for the briefest of moments, looking down at his corpse, with the smoking gun still in my hand, my victory felt very hollow indeed.

Fifteen years had passed since then.

I had watched, as we rebuilt humanity from its dying embers.

I had watched, as we brought back the ancient technologies that He had taken from us.

And I watched - not fully realizing what was going on - when we began to fight amongst ourselves.

It all began so innocently - small disagreements over rations, arguments over who deserved more.

Then it grew bigger. And bigger. Arguments turned into fistfights - fistfights went over the edge and the people howled for vengeance.

And before I knew it, the technologies of old were used in wars I did not wage.

That began merely four months ago.

And now, today - betrayal from my very own comrades.

Brother Anthony, who fought by my side for no less than twenty five years.

I coughed, and the faintest gurgles of a dying laugh echoed around the empty room. Perhaps the old man was right after all.
